knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A planned, protected one-way route avoids damage to lawns and paving.
A person entering the zone is a stop-work trigger. Stop, let them leave, restore the barrier, then restart.
Loose material on footpaths is a public hazard and can block stormwater drains.
The protecting the property section says to cover or move windows, doors and glass that could be struck by a branch, a blower or a thrown clipping.

practicalCriteria: Given a mock site plan, the learner draws a work zone, an exclusion zone and a one-way material route that does not cross the footpath, within the assessor's set time.
The learner places covers and marker stakes on mock windows and irrigation fittings before a simulated cutting task begins.
The learner stops a simulated cutting task when the assessor enters the zone, restores the barrier and restarts only when the zone is clear.
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Annotated mock site plan signed by the assessor.
Assessor observation record of the protection and barrier set-up.
Stop-event record for the simulated pedestrian entry.
stopWorkCriteria: Cutting while the assessor is inside the simulated exclusion zone.
Driving or standing equipment on a marked fragile surface.
Continuing after the barrier has been removed.
